picks.headline: Suno Inks ‘Strategic Partnership’ With Believe
picks.excerpt: AI music platform Suno has signed a strategic partnership with French music giant Believe, adding another major distributor to the licensed side of its business. Participating Believe and TuneCore artists can opt in to training, share revenue, and distribute AI tracks made with the licensed model.
picks.rationale: Third label partnership for Suno — opt-in training plus a TuneCore distribution path is a concrete new route to market for independent artists.

picks.headline: SoundBoost updates its browser-based mastering service with Engine v4
picks.excerpt: SoundBoost's Engine v4 lets you steer a master with plain-language instructions instead of assembling a mastering chain by hand. It renders a three-minute track in roughly ten seconds and accepts iterative refinement requests without restarting the job.
picks.rationale: Highest craft actionability in the pool — a rebuilt engine, a free tier, and a seed number that carries one master's character across a whole EP.

picks.headline: Jason Isbell Files Class Action Lawsuit Claiming Suno Coded AI to ‘Extract Musicians’ Identities’
picks.excerpt: Jason Isbell is leading a class action accusing Suno of encoding artists' musical personas as tokens so a name prompt returns identity-evocative output. The suit runs on rights of publicity rather than copyright, so it survives even where labels have already licensed recordings.
picks.rationale: Moves the legal fight from training data to the output side, and to a right artists own personally rather than through their labels.

picks.headline: Chartmetric launches AI agent Flow, priced from $60 per month: ‘Not just another AI chatbot’
picks.excerpt: Chartmetric has launched Flow, an AI agent that answers plain-language questions against its own music dataset, builds multi-phase marketing plans, and runs automations like alerts and shortlists. It cross-references 14 million artists and starts at $60 per month standalone.
picks.rationale: A working analyst-replacement agent for release strategy, with credits, tiers and pricing already public — directly changes how a manager preps a campaign.

picks.headline: Stella Parton urges people to stop creating AI ‘endless garbage’ about her late sister Dolly
picks.excerpt: Two weeks after Dolly Parton's death, her sister Stella asked on Instagram that people stop posting the wave of AI material about her. She called it a tremendous amount of AI and endless garbage that has been challenging to absorb or ignore.
picks.rationale: The posthumous-likeness problem stated by a family member, not a lawyer — the culture-side counterweight to this week's licensing and litigation news.
